1	import { breakpoints } from 'app/theme/foundation';
2	import { DRAWER_HEADER_ROW_HEIGHT } from 'app/theme/components/zimmDrawerShared';
3	
4	// Figma's actual named drawer sizes (SFCC-898) — five named sizes, not the three/four this
5	// file previously guessed at. Each name below matches Figma's own naming exactly, so there's
6	// no re-deriving which number belongs to which concept next time this file is touched:
7	//
8	//   Desktop Large — 50%  — Product Details, Filters (desktop width)
9	//   Tablet        — 80%  — Product Details, Filters (tablet width)
10	//   Desktop Small — 25%  — Notify Me, Wishlist, Find in Boutique, Regional Storefront,
11	//                           Cookies, Login
12	//   X-Large       — 82%  — Cart. SFCC-11: this is the named-size *library* annotation, not a
13	//                           measurement of the real Cart composition — see `WIDTH_XLARGE` below,
14	//                           which corrects it a second time against the actual frames.
15	//   Mobile        — unchanged, the baseStyle treatment every variant collapses to below `md`.
16	//
17	// An earlier revision of this file measured 82% off a Figma frame annotated "Tablet = 82% of
18	// screen" and used it as `small`'s (now `tablet`'s) value — that frame's annotation was wrong
19	// (or superseded): 82% is actually X-Large's value (Cart), a completely different drawer this
20	// codebase hasn't built yet, and Tablet is genuinely 80%. Corrected once confirmed directly
21	// against the list above, not another single frame's own label.
22	const WIDTH_LARGE = '50%';
23	const WIDTH_TABLET = '80%';
24	// The original width set when this drawer shell was first built (2026-08-27) — matches Figma's
25	// "Desktop Small" exactly. Used by every viewport-independent narrow utility drawer (Find in
26	// Boutique today; Notify Me/Wishlist/Regional Storefront/Cookies/Login once those exist).
27	const WIDTH_SMALL = '25%';
28	// SFCC-11 (Cart build): the "X-Large — 82%" library annotation two paragraphs up is the
29	// named-size *system* value, not a measurement of the actual Cart composition. Re-measured the
30	// real frames directly (node 9323:65888 at 1920px, node 9323:65895 at 1440px, file
31	// QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs) — the cart panel itself (frame "pdp/drawer") is a FIXED 1186px at
32	// both widths; the backdrop gap grows instead of the panel. 82% of 1920 is 1574px — 388px
33	// wider than designed. This is the same annotation-vs-measurement trap the comment above
34	// already records once for Tablet; it recurred here for X-Large. 74.125rem = 1186px.
35	// Widths/min-widths/max-widths across drawer sizes are a live, unsettled area as of
36	// 2026-09-17 (Marcel) — this ships to the current measured Figma spec and may be
37	// reconciled once that broader call is made; not a final word on the sizing model.
38	// audit-allow: Figma-confirmed fixed width with no --zimm-scale equivalent at this value.
39	const WIDTH_XLARGE = '74.125rem'; // 1186px
40	
41	// PDP drawer leaves a strip of backdrop visible below the panel on mobile (SFCC-736 AC 9,
42	// PO-approved 2026-08-21 — "so a user can easily navigate out"). Re-measured against node
43	// 40002218:42903 (SFCC-898): overlay 956px tall, panel 898px tall — exactly 58px. Only the
44	// `mobileGap` variant opts into this; the baseStyle defaults to full-height so utility
45	// drawers (wishlist auth, etc.) don't need to explicitly override it. No named spacing scale
46	// step lands on 58px — provisional raw value pending a foundation token.
47	const MOBILE_BOTTOM_GAP = '3.625rem'; // 58px
48	
49	// Close-button inset, measured from the pdp/drawer header frames. `tablet`/`small`/`xLarge`/
50	// `mobile` all share the same measured inset (32px/40px) at every width — only `large` switches
51	// to the wider 48px/64px inset, at/above the tablet breakpoint. Below that breakpoint `large`'s
52	// own override doesn't apply either, and the baseStyle inset is used instead, which is also how
53	// the whole drawer collapses to the mobile treatment on a narrow viewport regardless of `size`.
54	const INSET_COMPACT = { top: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)', right: 'var(--zimm-scale-2xl)' };
55	const INSET_LARGE = { top: 'var(--zimm-scale-1200)', right: 'var(--zimm-scale-4xl)' };
56	
57	// Header constants — from Figma drawer/header frame measurements.
58	// Compact horizontal inset (small/mobile): px=32px. Large desktop: px=64px.
59	// Small desktop header uses py=24px. Large desktop: container height=120px (row centred).
60	// Mobile base: container height=72px.
61	const HEADER_PADDING_COMPACT_X = 'var(--zimm-scale-2xl)'; // 32px
62	const HEADER_PADDING_LARGE_X = 'var(--zimm-scale-4xl)'; // 64px
63	const HEADER_PADDING_Y = 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)'; // 24px — small desktop py
64	// audit-allow: Figma-confirmed container heights with no --zimm-scale equivalents at these values.
65	const HEADER_HEIGHT_LARGE = '120px';
66	const HEADER_HEIGHT_MOBILE = '72px';
67	
68	export const ZimmDrawer = {
69	  parts: ['overlay', 'content', 'closeButton', 'header', 'headerTitle'],
70	  baseStyle: {
71	    // Explicit position/inset rather than relying on Chakra's own built-in `Drawer` overlay
72	    // styling — confirmed via inspection that it doesn't apply (renders `position: static`,
73	    // zero size) when the `<Drawer>` isn't given Chakra's own `size` prop, which this component
74	    // deliberately omits (see maxWidth note below). Owning it here avoids depending on that.
75	    overlay: {
76	      position: 'fixed',
77	      inset: 0,
78	      background: 'var(--zimm-color-opacity-50)',
79	      zIndex: 'overlay',
80	    },
81	    content: {
82	      // Chakra's own <DrawerContent> baked in a default white background
83	      // (@chakra-ui/theme's modal.js `baseStyleDialog`: `bg: colors.white`) that this recipe
84	      // never needed to set itself while that component was still in use — now that
85	      // ZimmDrawer hand-rolls its own content element (see index.tsx's file-level comment),
86	      // nothing supplies one unless it's set here. Matches Figma's pdp/drawer panel background
87	      // (bg-[var(--brand/color/palette/white,white)]) — --zimm-color-bg-07 resolves to the
88	      // same grey.white value (SFCC-898 — the panel briefly had no background at all).
89	      background: 'var(--zimm-color-bg-07)',
90	      width: '100%',
91	      // Matches `width` at every step below — Chakra's own `Drawer` theme defaults to
92	      // `size="xs"` (maxW 20rem) when no `size` prop is passed to `<Drawer>` (deliberate: its
93	      // fixed size scale has no 50%/25% steps), and that default `maxW` otherwise still caps
94	      // our own `width` override since we never reset it.
95	      maxWidth: '100%',
96	      // A `height` reduction, not a `bottom` offset — Chakra's own Slide transition (see
97	      // @chakra-ui/transition's slide.js `placement: 'right'` case) pins the sliding wrapper
98	      // with `position: fixed; top: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0`, a definite height. `bottom` on
99	      // this `position: relative` DrawerContent just shifts the box within that instead of
100	      // reliably opening a gap (SFCC-898 — mobile bottom gap wasn't rendering at all); a
101	      // percentage `height` resolves cleanly against that definite-height ancestor instead.
102	      // CodeRabbit (PR review): baseStyle should default to full-height so utility drawers
103	      // don't inherit the PDP-specific 58px backdrop strip — moved to the `mobile` variant.
104	      height: '100%',
105	      // Header stays fixed; only the content area (ZimmPdpDrawer's own `content` part) scrolls —
106	      // AC 10, "content area scrolls independently without the tab header scrolling".
107	      display: 'flex',
108	      flexDirection: 'column',
109	      overflow: 'hidden',
110	    },
111	    // Was missing `position: absolute` since this component's original commit — the
112	    // top/right insets below were silently no-ops (closeButton rendered as a normal in-flow
113	    // block instead of overlaying the header's corner), which is the root cause of SFCC-898's
114	    // close-button-misaligned-with-tabs defect across every breakpoint.
115	    //
116	    // height/display/alignItems/justifyContent: matches zimmTabs.css.ts's `menu.minHeight`
117	    // (DRAWER_HEADER_ROW_HEIGHT, zimmDrawerShared.ts) and centers the icon inside it — the
118	    // close icon's own intrinsic size doesn't equal the tab row's real rendered height, so
119	    // matching only `top` between the two (as before) left their vertical centers slightly
120	    // offset (SFCC-898, mobile). Only applies to the floating close button (no `title` passed) —
121	    // the inline title-row close button below is a normal flex child, not absolutely positioned.
122	    closeButton: {
123	      position: 'absolute',
124	      ...INSET_COMPACT,
125	      height: DRAWER_HEADER_ROW_HEIGHT,
126	      display: 'flex',
127	      alignItems: 'center',
128	      justifyContent: 'center',
129	    },
130	    // Drawer header — title (flex-1, left) + close button (right).
131	    // baseStyle applies the mobile/compact treatment: px=32px, container h=72px centred.
132	    // SFCC-926 (Figma): paddingBlock is 0 at mobile so the 72px minHeight controls the height
133	    // (flex centering handles vertical alignment). At md+ 24px block padding applies — matching
134	    // Figma's "small desktop py" spec without overriding the mobile 72px container height.
135	    header: {
136	      display: 'flex',
137	      alignItems: 'center',
138	      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)',
139	      backgroundColor: 'var(--zimm-color-text-inverse)',
140	      paddingInline: HEADER_PADDING_COMPACT_X,
141	      paddingBlock: 0,
142	      minHeight: HEADER_HEIGHT_MOBILE,
143	      flexShrink: 0,
144	      [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
145	        paddingBlock: HEADER_PADDING_Y,
146	      },
147	    },
148	    headerTitle: {
149	      display: 'flex',
150	      height: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)',
151	      alignItems: 'center',
152	      flex: '1 0 0',
153	      minWidth: 0,
154	      overflow: 'hidden',
155	      whiteSpace: 'nowrap',
156	      color: 'var(--zimm-color-text-default)',
157	    },
158	  },
159	  variants: {
160	    large: {
161	      content: {
162	        [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
163	          width: WIDTH_LARGE,
164	          maxWidth: WIDTH_LARGE,
165	          height: '100%',
166	        },
167	      },
168	      closeButton: {
169	        [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: INSET_LARGE,
170	      },
171	      header: {
172	        [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
173	          paddingInline: HEADER_PADDING_LARGE_X,
174	          minHeight: HEADER_HEIGHT_LARGE,
175	        },
176	      },
177	    },
178	    // Figma's "Tablet" size — the tablet-range step for Product Details/Filters, which
179	    // graduates to `large` (Desktop Large) at the desktop breakpoint via the caller's own
180	    // useBreakpointValue (ZimmPdpDrawer never selects this variant itself).
181	    tablet: {
182	      content: {
183	        [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
184	          width: WIDTH_TABLET,
185	          maxWidth: WIDTH_TABLET,
186	          height: '100%',
187	        },
188	      },
189	    },
190	    // Figma's "Desktop Small" — always narrow, at every width above the mobile collapse. No
191	    // js-level graduation to another variant the way `tablet` graduates to `large` — this is
192	    // the whole point for its utility-drawer consumers (Find in Boutique today).
193	    small: {
194	      content: {
195	        [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
196	          width: WIDTH_SMALL,
197	          maxWidth: WIDTH_SMALL,
198	          height: '100%',
199	        },
200	      },
201	    },
202	    // Figma's "X-Large" (Cart) — not consumed anywhere yet (Cart is a full page today, not a
203	    // drawer), but the real value is already here under the right name for when that changes.
204	    // `maxWidth: '100%'` (not WIDTH_XLARGE) so a viewport narrower than 1186px but still ≥ `md`
205	    // doesn't overflow.
206	    xLarge: {
207	      content: {
208	        [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
209	          width: WIDTH_XLARGE,
210	          maxWidth: '100%',
211	          height: '100%',
212	        },
213	      },
214	      header: {
215	        [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
216	          minHeight: 'unset',
217	          paddingBlock: HEADER_PADDING_Y,
218	        },
219	      },
220	    },
221	    // CodeRabbit (PR review): 58px backdrop strip is PDP-specific (SFCC-736 AC 9, PO-approved)
222	    // and must not apply to utility drawers — scoped here to the explicit `mobile` variant.
223	    // Figma's "Mobile" size — only drawers that need the strip opt in; utility drawers
224	    // (wishlist auth, etc.) use `large` instead, which collapses to full-height via baseStyle.
225	    mobile: {
226	      content: {
227	        height: `calc(100% - ${MOBILE_BOTTOM_GAP})`,
228	      },
229	    },
230	  },
231	};

## Bottom line

This commit ships exactly the drawer shell the plan asked for and nothing else — safe to merge on scope grounds. One real, cheap defect exists (wrong Storybook folder) and it's this commit's own job to fix before merge. The two things that look like defects on first read — the 1280-vs-1440 breakpoint and the FocusLock finding — are not scope problems: both were handled correctly given what was actually knowable at build time. I re-derived all of this from the diff and the plan source myself rather than trusting either report; specifics below.

**VERDICT: IN SCOPE** — 6 files, all in the manifest, all pass criteria evidenced. One non-blocking should-fix (Storybook category) flagged for correction before merge — it doesn't change the verdict because it isn't a manifest or tier problem, just a wrong label inside a file this commit correctly owns.

## What I independently checked (not taken on faith)

`git status --porcelain` / `git diff --name-only`: exactly one modified file (`overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`, +2 lines — an import and a registry-object key, nothing else) and one new folder with exactly 5 files (confirmed via `ls`): `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmCartDrawer/{index.tsx, zimmCartDrawer.css.ts, zimmCartDrawer.css.test.ts, index.stories.tsx, index.test.tsx}`. I read all 6 in full.

**Explicitly-out-of-scope items — confirmed absent, not just claimed absent:**
- `find` for any `useCartDrawer` hook anywhere in the repo → nothing.
- `git diff --stat` against `_app`, `_app-config`, `product-detail` → empty, untouched.
- `zimmDrawer/index.tsx` / `zimmDrawer.css.ts` → I read both directly; zero diff against them.
- Grep of the diff for every Tier 1 path pattern in the brief (`theme/foundation`, `ssr.js`, `worker/main.js`, root `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `babel.config.js`, `.github/workflows`, `CODEOWNERS`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/`) → no matches.
- The one Tier 2 file touched (`theme/components/index.ts`) is exactly the mechanical registration `overrideStyling.md` requires for any recipe, pre-authorized per the brief, and the diff is literally 2 lines.

**Ran myself, targeted (not the whole suite — Tester already ran that identically against this same unchanged diff, re-running it would be pure duplication):** `npx vitest run overrides/.../zimmCartDrawer` → `2 passed (2) / 15 passed (15)`, including the focus-restore test at 398ms. This resolves an ambiguous phrase in what was reported to me ("88/1263") — that's Vitest's own Test-Files/Tests dual counter from the full run, not a failing fraction; this component's own two files are 100% green.

## Question 2 — the 1280-vs-1440 breakpoint: disclosed, not silent

I read `.claude/session-notes.md` §11.1 and its "Responsive rule (derived)" table directly — this is where the plan's "desktop ≥1440" text actually comes from. It's an extrapolation from exactly two Figma frames (`cart/drawer/xlarge` at 1920px and `cart/drawer/large` at 1440px — both independently measured as an identical "1186 fixed" panel), with the next-nearest data point being `cart/drawer/tablet` at 834px. **There is no Figma frame anywhere in the plan's own source between 834 and 1440.** The "≥1440" number in the plan is itself a best-available inference, not a confirmed design threshold — so there was no way to *resolve* this ambiguity by re-reading Figma harder; it genuinely wasn't there to find.

Given that, reusing this codebase's own named `breakpoints.xl` (1280px, `gridSystem.ts`) instead of hardcoding a fresh, unbacked "1440" literal is exactly what `overrideStyling.md` already tells you to do when "no confirmed Figma value" exists for a dimension: reuse an established value rather than invent one. And it's disclosed loudly at the point of use (`zimmCartDrawer.css.ts:11-22`), including the honest caveat that it was "not independently re-verified against a Figma node by this commit." That's a reviewer catching this in ten seconds, not a landmine.

One tension worth naming rather than burying: Hard Rule #12 reads as "ask one clarifying question before writing any code," full stop, no low-stakes carve-out — a stricter reading says this should have paused before a single line was written, rather than documenting the assumption and moving on. I don't think that reading wins here, given the choice is a single reversible CSS threshold, produces zero functional breakage either way in the disputed range, and is flagged clearly enough for pre-merge correction — but I'm naming it rather than pretending the tension doesn't exist. Net: legitimate flagged-for-human-call, not a silent decision. This is a decision for you/design, not something either agent should resolve by guessing harder.

## Question 3 — FocusLock finding: correctly out of scope, and doesn't taint this commit's own tests

I read `zimmDrawer/index.tsx` directly (untouched by this diff, confirmed). The mechanism the Tester flagged is real and sits at lines 226-233: Chakra's own `ModalFocusScope`/FocusLock and this codebase's manual `handleCloseComplete` (fired via `onCloseComplete`) both act on the same close-transition timeline. Fixing that means editing `zimmDrawer/index.tsx` itself — a file this commit's brief explicitly bars touching, and doing it anyway would also trip Hard Rule #5 ("never refactor upward") and Hard Rule #10 (one tier/component boundary per change). Correctly left alone.

On whether this commit's *own* test should be rewritten: I read `index.test.tsx`'s focus-restore test myself. It runs the real `ZimmDrawer`/real Chakra Drawer/real framer-motion, nothing stubbed (the file has an explicit comment explaining why a framer-motion stub was tried and reverted), and asserts `toHaveFocus()` inside a genuine `waitFor`. That's not a test that passes regardless of behaviour — it would fail if focus weren't actually restored in jsdom. What it doesn't claim, and never did, is anything about real-browser paint/compositing timing — jsdom has no compositor, so no Vitest test, written any way, could observe the specific race the Tester found. The test's own framing ("exercises ZimmDrawer's actual logic") is accurate to what it can prove and doesn't overreach. So: no, surfacing the finding doesn't obligate a test rewrite here — there's nothing more truthful this file could say. The real gap is a missing real-browser (Playwright) assertion against the *shared* drawer mechanism, which is a different file's problem, not this commit's.

## Question 4 — the two should-fix items, judged on scope not severity

**Storybook category — this commit's job, now.** I grepped every organism under `ui-kits/organisms/`: `ZimmGalleryOverlay`, `ZimmProductCard`, `ZimmPdpDrawer`, `ZimmProductGallery`, `ZimmAuthDrawerContent`, `ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer` all file under `Commerce/`. `ZimmCartDrawer` alone sits under `Layout/` (`index.stories.tsx:8`). `components.md`'s own tiebreaker ("what does this component know about?") isn't ambiguous for something keyed on `itemCount`/`BAG • {n}` and an items/totals grid. Fixing this touches one string, inside a file this commit itself created — it doesn't reach outside the manifest, doesn't cross a tier, doesn't need anyone else's sign-off. It's in scope to fix before merge, and I'd fix it now rather than defer it.

**Unexported column constants — correctly left alone.** I read `zimmDrawer.css.ts` and its test directly: `WIDTH_XLARGE`/`WIDTH_LARGE`/`WIDTH_TABLET`/`MOBILE_BOTTOM_GAP`/header constants are all unexported, and `zimmDrawer.css.test.ts:29` hardcodes the resolved `'74.125rem'` literal rather than importing the constant — exactly the pattern `zimmCartDrawer.css.test.ts` follows for `ITEMS_COLUMN_WIDTH`/`TOTALS_COLUMN_WIDTH`. This is genuinely uniform with the live, shipping precedent, not a fresh shortcut. Fixing only the new file would make the new file *more* correct in isolation while creating a fresh disagreement between two recipe/test pairs doing the same job two different ways — nobody has decided the old pattern is wrong, so unilaterally deviating from it in one file is itself a small undisclosed scope call. Correctly left alone; worth a note for whoever eventually revisits both files together, not a fix owed by this commit.

- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer/zimmDrawer.css.ts` and `.css.test.ts:29` (unexported-constant precedent)
